summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, and a tracheostomy was admitted after a fall at his nursing home. He had lower abdominal pain and a positive urinalysis, leading to a diagnosis of a complicated urinary tract infection caused by Pseudomonas. He was initially treated with ceftriaxone, then switched to cefepime based on culture results. Imaging showed no acute trauma, and his chronic leg pain was unchanged. His abdominal pain improved with antibiotics. A midline was placed for IV antibiotic administration, and his foley catheter was exchanged. He remained stable, with no respiratory decline, and completed eight days of a ten-day cefepime course by discharge. He was discharged to extended care with plans to complete antibiotics and evaluate catheter necessity.
